title: QAOA for Max-Cut
summary: Max-Cut on a 5-vertex graph with a two-layer QAOA.
objectives: Turn a coloring of a graph into a bit string and the number of cut edges into an energy
Build alternating cost and mixer layers and train their angles
Compare the best ratio of one layer with two on the same graph
mission: Cutting more edges of this 5-vertex graph is a Max-Cut problem, and the circuit has to prepare a state whose expected cut is close to the best one. Build a QAOA circuit from Hadamards, cost layers (IsingZZ on every edge) and mixer layers (RX on every qubit), and optimize the angles until the approximation ratio of the state is above 0.85.

prediction.question: You find the best angles for one layer (p = 1) on this graph, then add a second layer and optimize all four angles again. What can you say about the best achievable ratio?
options: It cannot be lower than before: with both angles of the new layer at 0 the circuit is the p = 1 circuit, so that state is still reachable
It can be lower, because four angles are harder to optimize and the optimum moves
It stays the same, because both layers use the same cost Hamiltonian
prediction.explanation: A layer with γ = β = 0 is the identity, so every p = 1 state is also a p = 2 state and the best ratio cannot drop. The optimizer may fail to find it, but the best achievable value does not fall. It can rise, because the second layer reaches one edge further: on this graph it goes from about 0.82 to about 0.92.

hints: What does one layer do to a qubit and to an edge? The cost part acts on pairs of qubits joined by an edge, the mixer part acts on every qubit.
In layer(gamma, beta), apply qml.IsingZZ(gamma, wires=[i, j]) for each edge (i, j), then qml.RX(2 * beta, wires=wire) on each qubit. One layer is not enough to pass 0.85 on this graph.
Take params with one row (gamma, beta) per layer, so shape (2, 2) for two layers, and train with qml.AdamOptimizer(0.1) for about 80 steps. Append circuit(params) to history after each step.
